column1: # Classification for tests/llvm-test-suite.sh (WG-01, WG-02). Tab-separated rows of two kinds:
#       Portable code sees neither __linux__ nor __unix__ (ADR-14). The programs below choose their platform code by
#       those macros, so they build with -D__linux__ -D__unix__ -Dlinux -Dunix, as the SPEC benchmarks in the same
#       A known failure. The first matching row classifies it. Classes ending in "not-applicable" and starting with
#       "exclusion" are left out of the adjusted pass rate:
#         x86-not-applicable     the test exercises the x86 instruction set or x86 macros, which the portable target
#                                does not have by design (its data model is x86-64's, its code is CIL)
#         undefined-not-applicable  the test reads memory it never initialized, so its result depends on what the
#                                allocator hands out; it passes natively because a fresh heap is zero-filled
#         exclusion-fork         fork, which stays ENOSYS (owner decision 2026-10-31)
#         exclusion-glibc        glibc or libstdc++ behavior that musl and libc++ do not share (owner decision
#         exclusion-prototype    a call through a prototype that contradicts the definition, which llvmnet rejects
#       Every other class counts as a failure in both rates:
#         limitation             a documented limitation of llvmnet (docs/user/limitations.md)
#         backend-item           an open plan item, named in the reason
# A failure no row matches is "unclassified" and fails the test.
